title: Discovery catalogue
description:
The engine's DISCOVERY contract: what exists and what would run, computed with ZERO HTTP requests. Normative. `sample-catalogue.json` is illustrative only.

The catalogue is how the platform shows a user what will happen before anything happens, and how it joins run results back to test identities afterwards. JOIN ON THE IDs, NEVER ON POSITION - the generated inventory reshuffles rows and renumbers `Sr. No` whenever it is regenerated, and every id here is derived from content rather than position specifically so it survives that.

UPLOADED APIS NEVER APPEAR HERE. The engine is stateless; an upload travels by value inside the manifest and nothing is persisted. Use the applicability resolver to show which tests would run for one.

catalogueVersion.description: Version of the catalogue contract. Echoed into every result document so a consumer can tell which catalogue a set of results joins against.

apis.description: Every API in the generated inventory, sorted by `ref`.

testCases.description: The global set is published ONCE rather than duplicated under every API - it is the same checks for all of them, and repeating them per API would multiply the document by the inventory size for no added information. The size of the tier is deliberately not stated here: it grows as checks are added, so read the count off the `global` array rather than from this description.

global.description: The shared global-contract checks. Sorted by id.

apiSpecific.description: Checks belonging to one API - Newman assertions and generated checks. Sorted by id.

applicability.title: What would run, per API
applicability.description:
`ref` -> `testId` -> verdict. Computed statically, with no HTTP requests, so the platform can show it before a run.

The only legal transition at run time is `PLANNED` -> `NOT_APPLICABLE`; a test predicted `NOT_APPLICABLE` will never suddenly run. That direction is expected and is not an inconsistency - `test_content_type_negotiation` does it whenever an API returns a status nothing declared.

environments.description: The environments actually registered in this deployment, derived from the `<MODULE>_BASE_URL_<ENV>` keys - never a hardcoded list. Registering `ATTENDANCE_BASE_URL_QA` is all it takes to add `QA`. This is the set a manifest's `environment` is validated against at run time.

credentialAliases.description:
The credential LABELS registered in this deployment, so the platform can offer a valid choice instead of letting a user type one that is registered nowhere.

LABELS ONLY. Never a value, never a length, never a masked form - a masked value still leaks its shape and its existence.

classificationRules.title: The full result-state contract, as data
classificationRules.description: Everything a consumer needs to classify a result correctly WITHOUT reading any engine source. Published here precisely so the platform cannot re-derive it and get it wrong - re-deriving is how NOT_ASSERTED ends up counted as a pass.

reasonSeparator.description: What separates the state prefix from the detail in a raw reason string.

reasonFormat.description: How a raw reason string is composed. States travel as a structured PREFIX on the reason, which is what keeps them machine-readable downstream without a custom plugin.

classifyOn.description: What to classify on. Constant by contract: THE REASON PREFIX, never the pytest verdict.

classifyOnNote.description: The trap this closes, in prose: WARN and INFORMATIONAL are reported as skips because `pytest.skip` is the only built-in non-failing outcome carrying a machine-readable reason, but BOTH MEAN THE CHECK RAN. A consumer reading the pytest verdict records both as 'did not execute'.

states.description: All seven states with their definitions and their pass-rate membership. Exactly seven - a document with more or fewer is not this contract.

reasonPrefix.description: The prefix this state travels as. Equals `name`.

countsTowardPassRate.description: True for PASS and FAIL only.

executed.description: Whether the check actually ran. True for PASS, FAIL, WARN and INFORMATIONAL - the last two despite being reported as skips.

passRateDenominatorStates.description: THE ONLY TWO STATES THAT MAY APPEAR IN A PASS-RATE DENOMINATOR. Locked to this exact value by contract, sorted. If a consumer's denominator contains anything else, the consumer is wrong - most requests in the source collections carry no assertions, and counting those as passes makes the headline number a lie.

passRateExcludedStates.description: Everything else. Excluded from the denominator, still individually counted. Counting NOT_ASSERTED as a pass is the specific failure mode this guards against.

passRateNote.description: Prose restating that the rate is undefined when PASS + FAIL is zero - report 'not applicable', NEVER 100%.

executedStates.description: The states meaning the check actually ran against the API, sorted. WARN and INFORMATIONAL belong here even though pytest reports them as skips; treating them as 'did not execute' understates real coverage.

ref.description: THE JOIN KEY, and what a manifest's `ref` must match. `method|path|module|sub-module`, lowercased. Content-derived, so it survives the inventory being regenerated.

displayId.description: A display label such as `API-001`, scoped to whoever filled in the source sheet. NOT an engine identifier and never a join key. Currently `null` for every inventory row - emitted as null rather than invented.

path.description: Endpoint path as written in the source, host excluded. May carry URL-encoded template placeholders.

owner.description: Currently null for every inventory row. Emitted as null rather than back-filled with a guess.

sourceType.description: Which kind of collection this row came from. Determines whether its assertions are executable - see `assertionState`.

sourceCollection.description: Repo-relative path to the file this row was read from.

assertionState.description:
What is known about this API's own assertions:

  asserted              - assertions exist AND a runner executes them.
  asserted-not-executed - ASSERTIONS EXIST BUT NOTHING RUNS THEM.
  not-asserted          - the request runs; nothing asserts anything about it.
  unknown               - could not be determined from the source.

`asserted-not-executed` IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. A Bruno flow carries real `test(...)` blocks that the Newman runner never runs. Calling that `asserted` would show the platform assertions that cannot fire - the same failure as rendering an unasserted request green, just harder to spot. It is a PARTIAL state, not zero coverage: the generated tier still exercises these APIs. Render it distinctly from both neighbours.

id.description: Derived from the test FUNCTION name, never its title, so it survives any wording change.

title.description: Human-readable, read from the test's own decorator.

hostLevel.description: True for a check measuring a HOST or GATEWAY property rather than an endpoint property. These run ONCE PER DISTINCT HOST and are referenced by the other APIs behind it - applicability and results both say so, via `measuredBy`.

apiSpecificTestCase.title: One check belonging to a single API
apiSpecificTestCase.description: Two shapes: an ordinary case, and an ASSERTION-GAP placeholder carrying `assertionGap` and `expectedState`.

id.description:
Deterministic and free of run-specific data.

GENERATED ids derive from code identifiers and survive a title change. NEWMAN ids are TITLE-DERIVED and do not: a Postman assertion has no id and no stable position, and Newman reports results by assertion NAME, so the name is the only thing that can join. RENAMING A `pm.test()` STRING RETIRES ONE CASE AND INTRODUCES ANOTHER - history does not follow a rename. Reordering assertions is safe, which is the more common edit.

tier.description: `newman` - an assertion written in the collection. `generated` - a check the engine derives from the API's declared metadata. `endpoint` - a case authored by hand under test-cases/, which carries `source`.

assertionGap.description:
Present and true ONLY on a coverage-gap placeholder: a request that runs while asserting nothing.

This placeholder exists so the gap is VISIBLE. Showing '0 tests' for such a request reads as 'not covered yet'; showing this case reads as 'runs green while checking nothing', which is what is actually true and what someone needs to act on.

expectedState.description: What this placeholder will report at run time. Always `NOT_ASSERTED`, which is excluded from the pass-rate denominator - the gap is counted as a gap, never as a pass.

displayId.description: Per-endpoint case number, TC_001 upward in catalogue order.

source.description: Repository-relative path to the authored case file. Present on the `endpoint` tier only; generated and newman cases have no single source file.

category.description: How results are grouped for reporting. `coverage-gap` belongs to assertion-gap placeholders only. `business-rule` belongs to authored endpoint cases, which assert an API's own contract rather than a cross-cutting property.

applicabilityVerdict.title: Whether one check would run for one API

state.description:
What the catalogue can say BEFORE anything runs. Only these two - the other five result states are outcomes, not predictions.

`PLANNED` may still become `NOT_APPLICABLE` at run time. The reverse cannot happen.

reason.description: Why, for `NOT_APPLICABLE`. Empty string for `PLANNED` - present rather than omitted, so a consumer reads the same key either way.
